pr_body:
This commit adds:
  - the event definitions and logic for generating them,
  - the scheduling and jobs boilerplate to periodically log them.

Care is taken to redact all strings present in descriptors which might
unintentionally be leaking PIIs.

The event generation logic is tested on the schema of a bootstrapped
test cluster: the test checks that the events match expectations.

Fixes #84284.

Release note (general change): CRDB will now collect schema info if
phoning home is enabled. This schema info is added to the telemetry log
by a built-in scheduled job which runs on a weekly basis by default.
This recurrence can be changed via the sql.schema.telemetry.recurrence
cluster setting.  The schedule can also be paused via PAUSE SCHEDULE
followed by its ID, which can be retrieved by querying
SELECT * FROM [SHOW SCHEDULES] WHERE label = 'sql-schema-telemetry'.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/84761)

This change requires `google.protobuf.Any` support in `eventpb`. @knz may you, specifically, please take a look? I didn't worry about redaction at all (yet), my understanding is that the logical schema does not contain any PII. On that, and many other things, I may be wrong.

Thanks for taking a look on short notice! Much appreciated.

> Although I am raising my eyebrows at the introduction of the two SQL built-in functions: what do you suggest the UX will be?  Are we expecting users to call that themselves? 

Right now I'm the target audience: I'm using them mainly for prototyping and testing. I expect both will eventually be privilege-gated to admin roles. Perhaps the job creation one will eventually disappear and tests will instead rely on a programmatic interface to trigger its behaviour. The schedule creation builtin I expect to remain but never really be used, as is the case for the stats compaction schedule creation.

> What happens if they are called two times in a row?

The schedule creation builtin should be idempotent. What's missing is a hook in the server startup to ensure that the schedule exists, like the auto stats compaction schedule's `jobMonitor`, and perhaps also a hook in the schedule frequency cluster setting, again like the auto stats compaction. I've deferred writing that boilerplate until after getting some early validation :)

>This is, alas, incorrect. Even though we've made progress on schema identifiers (table/column names etc), you need to edit the literals out scalar expressions - DEFAULT, CHECK, scalar expressions inside view queries etc.

Ah, yes! I'd wondered about those. Will do.

> As to the actual code review, I'd invite you to ask Andrew for a more detailed scrutiny.

I will in due time. At this time, you've covered exactly the questions I was interested in and which blocked me. Thanks!
This is ready for review for a broader audience at this point.

> I think it's a mistake if the folks who are going to process this data downstream are not present in these reviews. 

I refuse to believe that adding a new structured log should be conditional on the whole pipeline being vetted beforehand. In what I imagine to be a sane world, the sink for new logs remains /dev/null or a bunch of rotated files or whatever, and whoever owns the ETL pipeline eventually opts in to consuming the new log into some sandbox warehouse. 

> Who are those folks?

We'll find out eventually, but the concern of log consumption by the data pipeline is at least somewhat orthogonal to log generation with the end-consumer in mind. The end consumer, right now, is me, for all intents and purposes.

> Are we absolutely certain we want elements?

No, but why do we have to be absolutely certain? I'm starting to get the impression that adding a new log stream is a sticky and expensive thing.

> How would you feel about supplying both the descriptors and the elements?

Sure, why not. I was hoping for some openness to a more iterative development style: what's wrong with reverting this PR before general availability if it turns out that this doesn't suit us, and putting up another? I don't think I'm being unreasonable in assuming that we're not going to get it right the first time around, which is why I went with the naivest thing possible (barring logging descriptors but I found working with elements easier)

> what's wrong with reverting this PR before general availability if it turns out that this doesn't suit us, and putting up another? I don't think I'm being unreasonable in assuming that we're not going to get it right the first time around, which is why I went with the naivest thing possible (barring logging descriptors but I found working with elements easier)

I'd feel better about that approach if I knew who was going to tell us we didn't get it right.

Let's narrow down the use cases for the sake of this PR: I want to be able to identify various forms of catalog corruption among our users, before these manifest themselves as validation failure in a patch upgrade or a stuck major version upgrade. This alone amply justifies the existence of this log.

For this purpose, I do in fact need to log unvalidated descriptors, so no more elements. I'll push something shortly.
I'm tagging @cockroachdb/jobs-prs for review of the first two commits which contain all the plumbing to auto-schedule a daily job of a new type.
I've future-proofed the test which queries `system.eventlog` in light of https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/84983 .
This is ready for another look, tl;dr I did everything you asked.

Thanks for taking a look @andreimatei! This all sounds reasonable, I'll do it.

>I'm surprised that I don't see an ID that's common to all events exported at once (a snapshot id?).
> For the purposes of the Obs Service (whose gonna ingest all telemetry events) but also for Snowflake and what not, I also imagined that there'd be an event record corresponding to the snapshot, with some metadata - e.g. a timestamp.

I can add a UUID identifying the snapshot, sure. I naively thought that the event timestamp (in the common fields) would be enough.

> I don't like this idea of this builtin. It seems random.

Great, I don't like it either. I just blindly copied what @cockroachdb/sql-observability did with `schedule_sql_stats_compaction()`. You might want to file a ticket in their board about this!

>I can add a UUID identifying the snapshot, sure. I naively thought that the event timestamp (in the common fields) would be enough.

One thing I'll say is that I'd like us to be able to paginate exporting the data in order to bound memory usage at some point in the future. If we do that, we can't pass all the events to the logging API at the same time and we definitely won't have a claim that they share a timestamp. I'm not certain they'd share a timestamp even if they were passed as a batch, and I don't think that's a great feature to depend on.
Sorry about the rebasing. This having already gone through several rounds of review, I was under the impression that it was close to being accepted.

I rebased and squashed this, this should be ready for another look. Sorry for keeping this stale for so long. I followed through on all the suggestions and promises. I added a hard cap on the snapshot size and some sampling for when we'd exceed it.

I use goroutines and channels to ensure and update the schedule and it's definitely much nicer this way, though I don't really know what I'm doing so please look at these changes in `controller.go` carefully. It seems to work, but who knows.

Quoting manually because for some reason Reviewable still won't work for me in this PR. I appreciate the thoroughness of this review. 

> who gets this error and what do the do with it?

You're right, it's dumb. ou can stop all these jobs simply by pausing the schedule. At this point it's just detritus from the auto stats compaction source code I copied. Removing.

> 100k seems really high to me. How about... 10k? Are we going to learn anything from the 10,001st table?

100k log events a week is a lot? I honestly don't understand. I'll reduce it to 10k as you prefer because I'm assuming you have good reasons to be afraid.

> you definitely don't want to log these to system.event_log, I don't think...
> Or to the dev channel.

You're definitely right about the dev channel. For the system table I was hoping that https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/84983 would have merged in the meantime. To be honest I'd forgotten all about this, thanks for noticing! Fixed

> speaking of which, what's the story with this kind of schedules and tenant clusters?

We want them there too (because why wouldn't we). Is this a particular cause for concern? I honestly have no idea.

> this chan needs a comment; can it be internal to Start() ?

yes and yes, will fix.

> why make the channel buffered if you block when it's full? 

no valid reason, will fix.

> hmmm... maybe keep retrying at some rate?

if you prefer. Will do.

> just SchemaDescriptor. It's describing a schema element, not a snapshot.

huh, indeed. Will do

> a built-in for tests? Is there no other way? Can't the code backing this built-in be copied to the tests?

Yeah, but what if I want to trigger the telemetry manually in a prod cluster? Seems like a legit use case for a builtin to me. I'm going to leave it in. If you feel strongly about this I can remove it during stability period. I'm running out of time now.

> https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/85643 has merged. This can now be cockroach.sql.sqlbase.Descriptor

Very nice! This is a welcome change. It's done. Ready for another look.
Seems like we've still got dependency cycles in the tests :(

This needs to ship now, it's time. I'm out of any after today until next week. It seems to me that what's still up for debate at this point is neither important nor urgent. I got rid of the import cycles, it wasn't too bad though it was an unwelcome waste of time considering the rather meager benefits of not having an `Any` in the logs.

> If an update comes while we're mid updateSchedule, we should update the schedule again. To achieve that, I think 1) you do want the channel to have a buffer of size 1 and we don't want to block here. Below is the idiom to not block if the channel is full.

Done! I didn't quite get what you meant the other day when you mentioned a select-default. This makes sense, thanks.

> I'm sad that this @weekly is going to end up being at literally the same time for every pod in the entire cluster. It'll mean that once a week, we create a ton of load on the logging infrastructure. Ideally we ought to find a way to spread out when in the week we do this logging. See https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/54537

If the logging breaks down because of a measly <1M events then we have bigger problems than not jittering the schedule, even though jittering is in fact desirable for other, better reasons.

> Honestly, I don't see a great reason to ever give up so long as you back off enough. I'd just turn this whole thing into a for look using the retrier, log on every failure, and set an initial retry to something on the order of seconds and back off up to something on the order 5-10 minutes.

Done. Out of curiosity: why is it better to retry indefinitely? That feels mildly dangerous somehow, more than the user's SET CLUSTER SETTING remaining without effect at any rate.

> Did you want to do anything about this?

@andreimatei is on vacation. I'm doing doing anything about this now. If this builtin is particularly offensive for whatever reason, a release blocker issue can be filed and addressed later on.

I'm still not sure what's up with CI, the failures are consistent, but not the same in bazel vs make...

> I've stated my unease, but will leave it at that.

If the beta gives cause for worry I won't have any problems reverting this PR if it's what it takes.

> aren't these just going to generally be dropped tables waiting for their GC ttl?

I hope so, but don't trust that this is always going to be the case.

> My reading of the winds is that it'd be desirable at some future point to redact constants as opposed to literally everything. Can you leave a TODO or file a follow-up issue?

I'll file a follow-up issue as soon as this is merged.
:+1: We definitely need to be cleverer about when to collect the snapshot, there's no doubt about that.
Thanks for the reviews. I filed https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/85788 and https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/85787 and tagged them as GA-blockers (because they are).

issue_context.title: job: add schema telemetry scheduled job
issue_context.body:
A scheduled job is the way to go as far as _within what_ the telemetry logging takes place.
As far as _what to log_ I'm currently leaning towards logging an element decomposition of each descriptor.
As for as _how much to log_ I currently intend to log all of it and we can retroactively add sampling policies and whatnot.

Jira issue: CRDB-17568
